newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir, Soyuz docked manually due to problem-official.
newsitem.headline: Mir, Soyuz docked manually due to problem-official.

text.p: Russia's Soyuz spacecraft carrying a relief crew had to dock with the troubled Mir space station manually because the automatic system had developed a fault, flight director Vladimir Solovyov said on Thursday.

He told reporters at Mission Control the fault occured when Soyuz was 13 metres (yards) from Mir. "Soyuz retreated by 25 metres and then docked manually," he said. "It was a technical malfunction. The situation was not a critical one but we will look into it."

Solovyov said a similar problem occured half a year ago when another Soyuz brought a new crew to Mir, including the current commander Vasily Tsibliyev. Solovyov gave no details of the incident which apparently was not made public at the time.

In a separate development, Solovyov said NASA astronaut, British-American physicist Michael Foale, would take part in a spacewalk scheduled for September 3 alongside new Mir commander Anatoly Solovyov (eds: no relation).
The space walk is meant to try and locate a hole in the Spektr module, pierced on June 25 when a supply ship crashed into it during a manual docking manoeuvre.
"The U.S. participation in Spektr repairs will be more active than we had expected," the flight director said.
